text:
Morgan: Quick follow-up on the spectral frag heatmap we talked about in the RFC meeting. I pushed a prototype collector that samples slab-level churn and emits a time-series heatmap. Wanted feedback on sampling cadence and what to surface in the console.
Anika: nice, can you link the proto? :eyes:
Morgan: https://git.internal/redwood/frag-tools/commit/ab12cd3 - main script is heatmap.py, it outputs csv per-slab frequency.
Rafael: high level Q — are we sampling allocations or reclaim events? sampling allocations will bias towards small short-lived, reclaim events bias long-lived holes.
Morgan: good point. prototype tags both. allocation_count and reclaim_count per slab + avg_unused_bytes.
Priya: for console UX I'd want: hotness score (0-1), fragmentation delta over last 5m, and a sparklines micro-chart per-slab. Heatmap overlay should be optional since it can be noisy.
Teo: cadence? current default is 1s which is expensive. For 1s we're adding ~6-8% CPU on p3 instances during soak. Maybe 5s or adaptive (increase sampling when hotness rises).
Sasha: +1 adaptive. Also prefer reservoir sampling for very high churn slabs so we don't blow memory with histograms.
dev-bot: CI pipeline triggered: perf/frag-heatmap (run 01) started by Morgan
Rafael: telemetry contract: include slab_id, node_id, tenant_id (anonymized), sample_ts, alloc_rate, reclaim_rate, unused_bytes, active_pages. Make tenant_id optional for privacy in hosted mode.
Morgan: agreed. Also thinking about spectral transform on the time series to find periodic eviction patterns (hourly spikes). That would drive prefetch/admission heuristics.
Priya: if we expose spectral score, show confidence band — ops will want to filter false positives.
Teo: implementation detail — do not attach full CSV to console; stream an aggregated JSON summary every minute and backfill raw samples to S3 for offline analysis.
Sasha: eviction policy hook idea: slabs with high spectral-p0 (persistent periodicity) => avoid demote during predicted reclaim window. Might reduce churn. Thoughts?
Rafael: sounds promising but risky. Need A/B test: can we simulate rollback if scheduling changes cause latency regressions?
Morgan: we can gate it behind a rollout flag per deployment and record p99/latency delta. If delta > 5% revert.
Priya: add alerting: heatmap hotness > 0.8 and p99 uplift > 3% => auto-disable spectral-driven scheduling.
Teo: minor: adjust sampling to 2s for dedicated nodes, 5s for hosted multi-tenant. Make it configurable via agent config.
Morgan: action items: 1) update collector to reservoir sample and anonymize tenant_id (Morgan), 2) add spectral transform pipeline sketch (Rafael), 3) UX mockups for heatmap + sparklines (Priya), 4) rollout gating + alerting (Teo).
Sasha: I'll prototype the gating boolean in the runtime so we can flip without deploy.
Morgan: thanks — will open a PR with the collector and a short doc. Expect a short demo next Thurs.
Anika: awesome, count me in for the demo.
Rafael: reviewing the spectral sketch today.
Morgan: (edited) one more: include a per-tenant coarse signal to help tenant-level autoscale recommendations but keep sample rate low for privacy.
Sasha: noted.
dev-bot: CI pipeline update: perf/frag-heatmap (run 01) completed — 8 tests passed, 2 flaky skipped
Priya: cool, thanks all :thumbsup:
